meta.title: The Cobbler's Bench
meta.skill_frame: Work out what a word means from the passage: use the sentence around it, not a dictionary guess.

reader.who: Students who read at about a third-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: Measured FK 2.9, 5.4, 5.3 (4.5 together) on the 3 parts. The load is a trade described through its tools, with two words, 'sole' and 'worn', used in their ordinary trade sense rather than explained. The last part asks the reader to read 'worth mending' as a judgment.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.text_status: Drafted for the band, review pending.
source.survey: A repair trade and its decline, so the reader has to take 'worth mending' as a decision about value, not a fact about shoes.
source.avoided: No prices, dates, or place names. No claim about how many cobblers remain.

session.difficulty_basis: Clue distance: the sentence supplies the job of each tool.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: A cobbler repairs shoes. He sits at a low bench with a box of tools beside him. The bench is low so the work sits close to his eyes and his hands can rest on his knees. The bottom of a shoe is called the sole. When a sole wears through, rain reaches the foot. The cobbler cuts a new piece of leather and glues it on, then sews the edge with heavy thread. The stitch is short and tight, so the new piece cannot curl up at the toe. A long, loose stitch would catch on a stair and peel the patch back within a week.
passage.part_2: Some repairs are quick. A loose stitch or a worn heel takes a few minutes. Others take a day, because the shoe must be taken apart first. The cobbler keeps the shape of the shoe with a wooden form while he works. Without the form, wet leather dries out of shape. He also keeps a drawer of old buckles and laces, because a customer often wants one small part and not a new pair. A single buckle can keep a good boot in use for another year, and the customer pays for the part, not the whole. A small part often decides whether a good boot is repaired or replaced.
passage.part_3: Few cobblers repair shoes today. New shoes cost less than a repair, so most people throw a worn pair away. A cobbler now is more likely to repair boots, bags, or belts, which cost more and last longer. The tools have not changed much. A cobbler today uses the same curved needle and waxed thread that a shop used a century ago, because the materials have not changed either. Leather still stretches, and thread still breaks where it rubs. The bench, the thread, and the short stitch still do the work. What changed is how often a person decides a thing is worth mending.

items.prompt:
The bottom of a shoe is called the ____.

Write the missing word.

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The bottom of a shoe is the sole.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The first part says the bottom of a shoe is called the sole.
tutor_only.tell: The word is sole. It is the bottom layer of a shoe.
help: Look at the third sentence of the passage.
It names the bottom of the shoe.

if_they_say.ask: The heel is at the back. What is the whole bottom called?

tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case and punctuation. Accept sole, including a clear misspelling such as sol.

items.prompt: What happens when a sole wears through?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. A worn-through sole lets the rain in.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The first part says when a sole wears through, rain reaches the foot.
tutor_only.tell: Once the sole is worn through, there is nothing between the foot and the wet ground.
help: Look at the sentence right after 'wears through'.
It says what gets to the foot.

if_they_say.when: the student says the shoe gets heavier
if_they_say.ask: The passage names what reaches the foot. What is it?

if_they_say.when: the student says the shoe falls apart
if_they_say.ask: Falling apart is not given. What comes through the hole?

not_required: how thick the new leather is

items.prompt:
New shoes cost less than a repair, so most people throw a ____ pair away.

Write the missing word.

tutor_only.confirm: Right. People throw a worn pair away.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The third part says new shoes cost less than a repair, so most people throw a worn pair away.
tutor_only.tell: The word is worn. A worn pair has been used until it is damaged.
help: Look at the second sentence of the last part.
The word describes the old pair being thrown out.

if_they_say.ask: New shoes are what people buy instead. What kind of pair is thrown away?

tutor_only.normalize: Ignore case and punctuation. Accept worn or worn out.

items.prompt: Why does the cobbler use a wooden form?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. The form keeps the shoe's shape as it dries.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The second part says the form keeps the shape of the shoe, and without it wet leather dries out of shape.
tutor_only.tell: Wet leather can dry crooked, so the wooden form holds the shoe in its proper shape.
help: Look at the two sentences about the wooden form.
The second one says what happens without it.

if_they_say.when: the student says the form makes the shoe bigger
if_they_say.ask: The passage does not mention size. What does the form hold?

if_they_say.when: the student says the form protects his hand
if_they_say.ask: No hand is mentioned there. What happens to wet leather without the form?

tutor_only.core_idea: To hold the shoe's shape while the wet leather dries.
accept_ideas: so the shoe does not dry out of shape
to keep the shoe in its shape
because wet leather can lose its shape
not_required: what the form is made of

items.prompt: What does the passage mean by worth mending?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. Worth mending is a judgment about whether repair makes sense.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The last sentence says what changed is how often a person decides a thing is worth mending, after the part explains that repair now costs more than a new pair.
tutor_only.tell: Worth mending means the item is valuable enough that fixing it makes more sense than replacing it.
help: Look at the last sentence, after the point about cost.
The passage says what changed is a person's decision.

if_they_say.when: the student says it means the shoe can be mended
if_they_say.ask: The passage says the question is whether a person decides it is worth it. What kind of decision?

if_they_say.when: the student says it means the cobbler is skillful
if_they_say.ask: Skill is not the point of the last sentence. What is the customer deciding?

tutor_only.core_idea: Whether the thing is valuable enough to repair instead of replacing.
accept_ideas: whether a repair costs less than a new one
if the item is good enough to save
